newsitem.title: TURKEY: No plan for Ciller to quit coalition - Turk minister.
newsitem.headline: No plan for Ciller to quit coalition - Turk minister.

text.p: A minister in the conservative wing of Turkey's government said on Friday he did not expect Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller to quit the Islamist-led coalition.

The Yeni Yuzyil daily on Friday quoted unnamed cabinet ministers as saying Ciller, also the foreign minister, had decided to pull her True Path Party (DYP) out of the 10-month-old government in the latest twist of a deepening row between the government and the army.
But True Path officials could not confirm the report.
State Minister Salim Ensarioglu, a member of True Path, said he was unaware of any attempt by Ciller to ditch government partner Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader.
"I have no information on such a decision. I don't expect a withdrawal," he told Reuters.
Turkish stocks were up slightly in early trade on Friday. Shares dropped 4.9 percent on Thursday on fears the alliance with was crumbling.
"The feeling among the DYP is that Ciller has definitely decided to pull out," wrote Yeni Yuzyil columnist Bilal Cetin, a leading political analyst.
Ciller's faction is uneasy at the Erbakan's failure to implement an anti-Islamist crackdown demanded by the powerful army.
Erbakan will face the generals at a meeting of the National Security Council on Saturday that has been billed as a showdown.
The prime minister and the fiercely secularist army have been at loggerheads since February when the generals told him to curb the growing role of Islam in public life.
The government has taken no concrete steps to comply with the army's demands, which include restrictions on religious education, and strict enforcement of bans on Islamic dress.
The row heightened on Thursday when Erbakan said he would ask military headquarters to take legal action against a general who called him a pimp last week.
The Hurriyet daily said on Friday that a True Path cabinet member sympathetic to the army had told Ciller he would resign if she did not abandon the coalition.
"If we resign the government will go and you will be left in the lurch," it quoted Trade and Industry minister Yalim Erez as telling Ciller.
